correctness.rationale: The cited Xu modal-ordering theorem identifies Gamma_{3,q}=(2π)^3(I_0(q)^{2/q}−I_1(q)^{2/q}) for q>3. At ν=1/2 the Bessel modes are c sin r/r and c(sin r−r cos r)/r², c=√(2/π). The first has unique absolute maximum at boundary r=0 with log profile −r²/6, producing I0=c^q C0 q^-3/2(1+O(1/q)); the second has unique interior absolute maximum r*≈2.08157598 where N(r)=(r²−2)sin r+2r cos r=0 and v''=−(1−2/r*²)v*, producing I1=(cv*)^q C1 q^-1/2(1+O(1/q)). Exact tails show no other peaks dominate. Taking 2/q powers and subtracting yields log rate 16π²(3−v*²) and full constant term. Independent root solving found r*=2.0815759778181007, Gamma∞≈127.86987173622556, rate≈443.69721257108506, and numerical quadrature at q=64,128,256 approached the claimed two-term asymptotic. Published finite-q modal premise is not established by numerics.
